what is islam: Islam is a monotheistic religion founded in the 7th century by the Prophet Muhammad. Its central belief is in the oneness of God, known as Allah, and its holy book is the Quran. The basic principles of Islam include the declaration of faith, prayer, fasting, charity, and pilgrimage to Mecca. Muslims believe in accountability and the afterlife, and the religion emphasizes social justice, equality, and respect for all human beings. It has over 1.8 billion followers worldwide and is one of the largest and fastest-growing religions in the world.
islam: Islam is a monotheistic religion founded in the 7th century by the Prophet Muhammad in the Arabian Peninsula. The central text of Islam is the Quran, believed to be the word of God as revealed to Muhammad. Muslims believe in the oneness of God and follow the Five Pillars of Islam, which include the declaration of faith (shahada), prayer (salah), charity (zakat), fasting during Ramadan (sawm), and pilgrimage to Mecca (hajj) for those who are able. Islam teaches that all people are equal before God and promotes peace, justice, and compassion towards others. Today, Islam is the second-largest religion in the world, with over 1.8 billion followers.
Taqlid: Follow the guidance and teachings of recognized Islamic scholars and authorities, while also using critical thinking and reason to understand and interpret the religion.
Hajj: Make the pilgrimage to the holy city of Mecca at least once in a lifetime, if physically and financially able to do so.
Ihsan: Strive for excellence in all aspects of life, including worship, work, and relationships with others.
Sabr: Practice patience and endurance in the face of adversity, and trust in Allah's plan and wisdom.
Taubah: Seek forgiveness from Allah for one's sins, and make a sincere effort to avoid committing them again in the future.
Dawah: Share the message of Islam with others in a respectful and compassionate manner, and invite them to learn more about the faith.
Shariah: Follow the Islamic legal system, which governs all aspects of life including family, business, and criminal law.
Hijab: Wear modest clothing and cover one's hair for women, as a symbol of modesty and piety.
Ijtihad: Strive for intellectual effort to understand Islamic teachings and apply them in modern times.
Adab: Respect and show proper etiquette towards elders, parents, and others in authority.
Jihad: Strive to improve oneself and society through peaceful means, and defend Islam and Muslims when necessary.
Sadaqah: Give voluntary charity and perform good deeds to please Allah and help others in need.
Halal: Consume only foods that are permissible under Islamic law, and avoid those that are haram (forbidden).
Haram: Avoid all activities, substances, and behaviors that are forbidden in Islam, such as gambling, drinking alcohol, and illicit sexual relations.
Fitrah: Recognize the innate human nature to believe in Allah and follow His guidance, and seek to live a life in accordance with that nature.
Tazkiyah: Purify one's heart and soul through self-reflection, repentance, and spiritual growth.
Khushu: Develop a deep sense of humility, awe, and reverence in prayer, and focus on the presence of Allah.
Muamalat: Conduct business and financial transactions in an ethical and fair manner, and avoid any practices that exploit or harm others.
Hikmah: Use wisdom and discretion in all actions and decisions, and avoid unnecessary conflict or harm.
Fard: Fulfill all obligatory duties in Islam, including prayer, zakat, fasting, and hajj, as well as other obligations such as honoring parents and being truthful.
Mujahada: Strive to overcome personal weaknesses and bad habits, and seek self-improvement through discipline and effort.
Haya: Cultivate a sense of modesty, humility, and shyness in one's interactions with others, especially in matters of personal and private nature.
Salat: Perform the five daily prayers, which are obligatory for all adult Muslims who are physically and mentally able to do so.
Zakat: Give charity to the poor and needy. Muslims are required to donate a certain portion of their wealth to charity each year.
Sawm: Observe fasting during the holy month of Ramadan. Muslims fast from dawn until dusk and abstain from food, drink, and other physical needs during this time.
Tawheed: Believe in and worship Allah as the one and only God, and reject all forms of idolatry and polytheism.
Akhlaq: Practice good character and manners, including honesty, humility, kindness, and respect for others.
